explanation: Fires on the second subword piece of a word whose first piece is "St"/"st"/"Christ" (e.g. Christ|al, ST|AP, nyst|agmus, St|ew, Bundest|ag, Nest|lé, Standard|Error, polycryst|alline); the continuation token after a 'st'-ending fragment is key. Other word-internal continuations fire weakly.

Fires on mid-clause function/verb tokens in narrative or news prose, especially particle-verb or phrasal constructions ("sign up", "signed up", "dropped out", "found out", "fell through", "fear of", "followed by an"). No clear lexical trigger; moderate activity spreads across ordinary prose tokens.

A mixture: separators inside enumerated or tabulated items (colons in MAC addresses, the token before 'd)' in multiple-choice lists, the space before a number), the word 'soil'/'earth' in environmental text, and assorted code punctuation. No single shared feature.

Fires on the second token of a word split after a short first piece, mostly the prefix 'hydro' in scientific compounds (hydrophobic, hydrolysis, hydroxylation), 'k' in Hokkaido and 'Mort' in names/words (Mortimer, Morty, mortos), plus pieces of proper names (Kirtley, Hertsgaard, Bracken). Weak on code tokens.
A mixture: 'public'/'private' in cryptography or class-access contexts, 'SHALL' in 'IN NO EVENT SHALL' license boilerplate, and many unrelated biomedical, place-name and code tokens.

Fires on the noun or adjective right after a quantity or multiplicity word ('many/several/14/a number of [different]', 'number of [teams/nodes]', 'multi-[user/Channel]'), and on 'on'/'to' in 'a lot going on' and 'a lot to learn'. Marks plurality or variety; strongest on 'different' after a quantifier.

Fires in programming contexts (code, code comments, Q&A answers about code) on tokens that start a comment or line or give advice: '# TODO', '//', indentation, '{' at the start of a function body, and phrases like 'you might want to try'. Strongest on comment markers and TODOs in source code; near zero in non-technical prose.

A mixture: the space before the second number in an 'X (a, b)' breakdown of counts (girls/boys, males/females), the word 'much' in 'much like/much less/much to', and words in software license boilerplate ('except', 'WITHOUT', 'The above').

Fires when a name or element seen earlier in the text is mentioned again: the later continuation pieces of a recurring person's name (K|ieran, Razz|az, Cost|igan, K|immel) and HTML closing-tag names (, , ) that repeat an earlier opening tag. Repetition of an earlier entity is what matters.

Diffuse mixture: the second pieces of first names (Rach|ael, Miche|le, Brend|an), algebra variable tokens like '*z' or '*h', include paths, Cyrillic word pieces and assorted code tokens. No shared concept.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word that the tokenizer splits, especially a capital initial or short onset that starts a proper name or acronym (Nich|olson, non-H|odgkin, P|altrow, Ste|vie, Bis|accia, L|inq). Strongest when this first piece cannot be predicted from the context.

A mixture centred on scientific and technical writing: physics/cosmology abstract terms ('accelerating', 'cosmic background', 'upper bound', 'full width'), '+/-' in reported statistics, and assorted header, address and code pieces.

Fires on the '0' token directly after the thousands comma in large numbers (e.g. 231,|0|00 or 3,|0|58), with strongest activity on population, money and count figures. A token right after a comma in other sequences (', with', ', making', '2',3') fires moderately.

Fires on the separator inside a time-of-day or timestamp, i.e. the ':' (or '.') right after the hour digits (10:30, 3:25 PM, 2019-04-08 08:18). Weaker on separators in version numbers and other numeric strings.
